findings.title: Unrelated 10x increase in cleanup frequency
findings.body: The ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no mention in the PR description. This runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x as often, increasing DB and I/O load cluster-wide. Revert unless intentional.

findings.title: Debug logging left at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log at r.log.Error on every batch, including the full ids slice, cond and err (lines 534,537,554,557,576,579). A batch can hold tens of thousands of IDs, so every cleanup run will spam error logs and can blow up log volume/storage. These should be Debug or removed before merge.

findings.title: Split fetch/delete can exit early leaving work undone
findings.body: untilDoneOrCancelled stops when a batch returns affected==0. With the new two-step flow a batch can fetch non-empty ids but have deleteByIDs report 0 RowsAffected due to a concurrent deleter already removing those rows. The loop then returns success while matching rows still remain, deferring them to the next cycle or stalling max-count enforcement. Termination should be based on empty fetch, not zero rows-affected.

findings.title: SQLite fallback builds IN-list quadratically and on wrong condition
findings.body: The SQLite large-batch path is chosen when cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999 rather than len(ids) > 999, so small trailing batches still take the string-interpolation path. Worse, it builds the list with repeated fmt.Sprintf in a loop, which is O(n^2) copying for batches up to 32767 IDs. Check len(ids) and use strings.Builder.
